newsitem.title: FRANCE: DHL plans intra-Euro A300 freighters this.
newsitem.headline: DHL plans intra-Euro A300 freighters this.

text.p: DHL Aviation, the air transport arm of the DHL group, said it hoped to be operating Airbus 300 freighter aircraft on its intra-European services later this year.

"We would like to introduce A300Fs during the Autumn to take the strain on capacity in the peak final quarter of the year. However, there is some doubt on when the aircraft we have earmarked to use will be given the go-ahead for commercial service by the relevant mandatory authorities," a Brussels-based DHL Aviation official told Reuters.
DHL Aviation was in discussions with a number of aircraft leasing operators, among them Channel Express, the official said.

"We are talking with Channel Express on the possibility of leasing its A300F for night-time flights. But the company is still awaiting FAA approval on cargo conversion work which was completed around two months ago."

DHL Aviation also had its eye on several A300s currently being converted by Daimler-Benz in Dresden and British Aerospace in Filton, on behalf of of U.S. leasing companies, Pinnacle Aviation and CS Aviation.

"The completion of conversion work on these four aircraft ranges from June to September 1997 after which time they will have to gain approval to operate from the competent bodies. So we really can't say when they will be available for service."
The A300F had a cargo capacity of between 40 and 45 tonnes with an operating range of between 1,600 and 2,000 miles, the official added.

"Within the next month we are going to have to make a decision on where the extra capacity to see us through the September-December peak is coming from. A favourable turn of events would allow us to introduce a couple of A300Fs in the Autumn but clearly this depends on factors beyond our control."
DHL Aviation had already made plans to operate a further two Boeing 727Fs this Autumn and more aircraft of this type would be considered if the A300Fs were unavailable during the period in question.
DHL currently deploys around 25 727Fs on intra-European routes.

"We're achieving annual growth in the volume of traffic of between 25 and 30 percent and we simply need bigger planes and the gradual build-up of four to five A300F fleet would fit the bill while maintaining our 727F fleet."
DHL Aviation is part of the DHL Worldwide Express group whose main shareholders are Lufthansa and Japan Airlines.
